day_shape: 76 items: JD Vance announces CENTCOM–IRGC direct talks in Qatar, cargo ship struck in Strait of Hormuz, four IDF soldiers wounded in south Lebanon clash, three UK Parliament Iran questions tabled, heavy regime Ashura/Karbala messaging cycle.

threads.label: CENTCOM–IRGC Qatar track and MoU fallout
threads.summary: JD Vance announced that CENTCOM and the IRGC will meet directly in Qatar for conflict-resolution talks, while the IAEA chief said the US-Iran accord grants inspector access despite Iranian reservations. Iranian MP Mahmoud Nabavian denounced the memorandum on state television, and a Quinnipiac poll found 60% of US voters said military intervention in Iran was not worth it.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz ship attack and corridor dispute
threads.summary: A cargo ship was struck by a projectile off Oman, with the IRGC stating safe passage requires Iran-designated routes. An ultraconservative Iranian outlet warned that Oman's IMO-coordinated temporary shipping corridor could challenge Iran's Hormuz position, while a separate report said Tehran eyes Turkey's Dardanelles taxation model.

threads.label: South Lebanon clashes and buffer-zone dispute
threads.summary: Four IDF soldiers including two officers were wounded in a Hezbollah clash overnight, a reserve soldier (Master Sgt. Basil Sweid, 32) died in an operational accident, and the IDF said it killed six Hezbollah operatives in Zawtar al-Sharqiya and Ali Taher. A US State Department official said Israel had withdrawn from parts of the buffer zone as a good-faith step, which Israeli military officials denied; Defense Minister Katz said forces would remain in Lebanon, Syria and Gaza without time limit.

threads.label: Hezbollah and IRGC Quds Force messaging
threads.summary: Hezbollah Secretary-General Sheikh Naim Qassem said Israel must completely withdraw from Lebanon and thanked Iran for assistance in creating deterrence, while IRGC Quds Force commander Esmail Qaani warned Israel must withdraw today or face defeat tomorrow. Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters said Israeli aircraft movements in neighbouring countries' airspace constituted a threat the Islamic Republic would not tolerate.

threads.label: IRGC overseas operations exposed
threads.summary: Montenegrin police and the FBI arrested an Iranian-Turkish national wanted over IRGC-linked cyberattacks on more than 150 US universities, while Australia's domestic spy chief said the IRGC used two former Australia-based agents to direct arson attacks on Jewish targets in Sydney and Melbourne. Canadian security agencies flagged an Iranian doctoral student at Carleton University as a national-security threat over aerospace research.

threads.label: Ashura cycle and slain-leader funeral logistics
threads.summary: IRIB and Defa Press ran a heavy Ashura/Karbala messaging cycle including Foreign Minister Araghchi's post pledging never to forgive Khamenei's killing, and Khamenei's office published mourning-ceremony footage from 9–10 Muharram. Tehran Municipality launched a 'Bale' app registration platform for non-Tehran pilgrims attending the funeral of the martyred leader, while Iran International reported government supporters and opponents used the rituals for competing messaging.

threads.label: UK Parliament Iran questions tabled
threads.summary: The Lord Bishop of Chelmsford tabled three Iran questions to the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office covering expulsion of Afghan refugees from Iran since the recent conflict, UK aid levels to Iran and the region, and whether Iran has contravened the ICCPR since the start of US-Israel-Iran hostilities. The questions were tabled on 25 June 2026.

events.title_en: South Korea's programme to produce indigenous version of Iran's Shahed 136 drone
events.summary_en: South Korea's programme to produce indigenous version of Iran's Shahed 136 drone. South Korea has announced its programme to develop and deploy low-cost suicide drones modelled on Iran's Shahed 136 drone. South Korea's Defence Ministry announced that these indigenous suicide drones have been developed through reverse-engineering of Iran's Shahed 136 drone and are set to enter operational service as part of this country's drone capability enhancement programme. In addition, South Korea's military intends to purchase over 20,000 low-cost drones including short-range reconnaissance drones and loitering munitions.

events.title: Four IDF soldiers, including two officers, were injured in a clash with a Hezbollah gunman in southern Lebanon last night, the military says. A combat officer was moderately hurt in the incident, and another officer and the two soldiers were lightly hurt, the IDF says. They were taken to the hospital for treatment, and their families were notified. According to an IDF probe of the incident, at around 10 p.m. last night in the Beit Yahoun area, a Hezbollah operative who was hiding in a building threw a grenade at Israeli troops, causing the injuries. Within a few minutes, the forces returned fire, killing the operative, the probe finds. The IDF also struck several Hezbollah sites in the area

"We will not compromise on Israel's supreme security interest: protecting our soldiers and safeguarding our citizens, and we will not withdraw from the security zones," Katz says at the officers' school in southern Israel, known as Bahad 1. He also warns Tehran that if "Iran attacks Israel because of our actions in Lebanon, or for any other reason, we will strike it with full force."

events.title: Security Council, 10183rd Meeting (PM) UN Disengagement Observer Force
events.summary: At 3 p.m., the Security Council will vote on a draft resolution renewing the mandate of the UN Disengagement Observer Force (UNDOF), which expires on 30 June. UNDOF was established following the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement between Israel and Syria, which ended the Yom Kippur War. Its mandate is to maintain the ceasefire between the parties and supervise the disengagement of Israeli and Syrian forces, as well as the areas of separation and limitation in the Golan.

events.title: Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement: Small Purchase Exception for the Acquisition of U.S. Flags (DFARS Case 2024-D013)
events.summary: DoD is proposing to amend the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) to implement sections of the National Defense Authorization Acts for Fiscal Years 2024, 2025, and 2026. These sections provide a requirement for full domestic production of flags of the United States acquired by DoD, amend an exception to the requirement to buy certain articles from American sources, and expand the domestic sourcing requirement for seafood acquired for commissary resale.

events.title: Agricultural Foreign Investment Disclosure Act of 1978
events.summary: The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is proposing to update its regulations regarding the Agricultural Foreign Investment Disclosure Act of 1978 (the AFIDA). The revisions would reflect Congressional directives to establish a streamlined process for electronic submission and retention of disclosures made under AFIDA, including the deployment of an internet database. It would also revise reporting requirements and strengthen enforcement measures. Through the implementation of modernization measures and expanded scope and depth of reporting, this proposed rule will help ensure the AFIDA regulations address foreign investment and ownership of American agricultural land, particularly as it might present a national security risk.
